chunks: O you who believe, turn to God truly in repentance. Perhaps your Lord may forgive your ills and admit you to gardens with rivers flowing by on the day when God will not humiliate the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will move in front of them and to their right, and they will say: 'O Lord, perfect our light and forgive us. You have power over every thing.'
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of sincere repentance (Tawbah Nasuha) and the promise of light on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Tawbah Nasuha' (sincere repentance) is distinguished by its consistency and depth, often linked to the intercessory role of the Ahl al-Bayt. The verse culminates in a supplication for the perfection of 'Nur' (light), a concept central to Shia theology regarding the spiritual illumination of the Prophet and the Imams. This connects the individual believer's repentance to the cosmic reality of divine light that guides the faithful on the Day of Judgment.
